claims.text: Standard thermo-mechanical processing produces conventional metallic alloys with homogeneous microstructures.
Machine-learning-guided optimization can identify thermo-mechanical processing parameters that reliably induce gradient or bimodal microstructures.
A stepwise thermo-mechanical schedule can create controlled spatial variations in grain size within conventional alloys.
The resulting microstructure contains alternating ultrafine-grained and coarse-grained regions.
Ultrafine grains increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Adjacent coarse-grained regions preserve ductility by facilitating dislocation mobility.
Synergistic interaction between ultrafine- and coarse-grained regions decouples the conventional strength-ductility trade-off.
The proposed processing route simultaneously enhances strength and ductility relative to homogeneous processing.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength than a conventionally processed homogeneous baseline.
The treated alloy will maintain or improve ductility relative to a conventionally processed homogeneous baseline.
Increasing alloy strength commonly comes at the cost of reduced tensile ductility.
Standard homogeneous thermo-mechanical parameters are responsible for the baseline strength-ductility trade-off.
The proposed method is applicable to alloys amenable to thermo-mechanical processing.
The proposed strength and ductility benefits apply under room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The method's effectiveness in extreme environments remains unestablished.
Formation of the gradient microstructure may not be reproducible because of processing and material-response variations.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the method can reliably induce gradient or bimodal microstructures, while the uncertainty field says reproducibility of their formation is uncertain.

The predicted outcome permits ductility to be merely maintained, but the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and ductility; a result with increased strength and maintained ductility would therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.
